title: Converting compound units (speed)
problem: Convert 108 km/h to metres per second.

steps.instruction: Convert km/h to m/s by converting km → m (multiply by 1000) and h → s (divide by 3600).
Note the reverse conversion, from m/s to km/h.
steps.working: To go from m/s to km/h, multiply by 3.6.

title: Fuel consumption
problem: A car uses 52.5 litres of fuel to drive 700 km. Petrol costs \$2.05 per litre. (a) Find the fuel consumption in L/100 km. (b) Find the cost to drive 400 km.

steps.instruction: Part (a): find the fuel consumption in L/100 km.
Part (b): use the consumption rate to find the litres needed for 400 km.
Multiply the litres by the price per litre to find the cost.

answer: (a) The fuel consumption is 7.5 L/100 km. (b) The cost to drive 400 km is \$61.50.

title: Energy rates in context
problem: A gym session burns 420 kJ in 20 minutes, then the person rests and burns 80 kJ in 40 minutes. (a) Find the burn rate during exercise in kJ/min. (b) Find the burn rate at rest in kJ/min. (c) Find the average burn rate over the full hour.

steps.instruction: Part (a): find the exercise burn rate.
Part (b): find the rest burn rate.
Part (c): find the total energy and total time, then the average rate.
steps.working:
Total energy = $420 + 80 = 500$ kJ. Total time = $20 + 40 = 60$ min.
$$\text{Average rate} = \frac{500}{60} = 8.3\overline{3} \approx 8.33 \text{ kJ/min}$$

answer: (a) 21 kJ/min during exercise. (b) 2 kJ/min at rest. (c) Average rate over the hour ≈ 8.33 kJ/min.
